knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=Input data frame of mutations with columns sample, chrom, start, end, ref, alt ;; reference=BSgenome object representing the reference genome ;; x=Matrix of mutation counts (patients as rows, 96 trinucleotide categories as columns) ;; K=Number of signatures or range of numbers of signatures to extract ;; background_signature=Background signature matrix to be incorporated ;; lambda_values=Numeric vector of LASSO penalty values to test for sparsifying beta ;; beta=Initial values of beta to be used during estimation ;; seed=Random seed for reproducibility
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Appropriate when analyzing somatic point mutation data from cancer genomes to discover de novo mutational signatures while controlling for background mutation processes and enforcing sparsity.
- pitfalls: Choosing a LASSO penalty (lambda) that is too small can lead to dense signatures, while a value that is too high can result in a poor fit of the observed counts. Cross-validation (nmfLassoCV) can be extremely time-consuming and memory-intensive; the documentation advises using parallel execution and splitting the cross-validation into multiple independent runs (e.g., 10 independent runs of 10 iterations instead of one run of 100 iterations) to reduce memory requirements. If the likelihood is not increasing during nmfLasso, a warning will suggest trying a lower value of lambda.

workflows.name: mutational_signature_discovery
workflows.intent: Extract and visualize de novo sparse mutational signatures from patient point mutation data.
input: ssm560_reduced (data frame of somatic point mutations with columns sample, chrom, start, end, ref, alt)
workflows.stages: 1. Load mutation data and reference genome ;; 2. Convert mutation data to a 96-trinucleotide count matrix using import.trinucleotides.counts ;; 3. Plot patient mutation counts using patients.plot ;; 4. Estimate starting beta values using startingBetaEstimation ;; 5. Evaluate the range of LASSO penalty values using lambdaRangeBetaEvaluation ;; 6. Perform cross-validation to select the optimal number of signatures (K) and lambda using nmfLassoCV ;; 7. Extract signatures using nmfLasso with the selected parameters ;; 8. Plot the discovered signatures using signatures.plot
workflows.code:
library("SparseSignatures")
data(ssm560_reduced)
head(ssm560_reduced)
library("BSgenome.Hsapiens.1000genomes.hs37d5")
bsg = BSgenome.Hsapiens.1000genomes.hs37d5
data(mutation_categories)
head(mutation_categories)
imported_data = import.trinucleotides.counts(data=ssm560_reduced,reference=bsg)
head(imported_data)
patients.plot(trinucleotides_counts=imported_data,samples="PD10010a")
data(patients)
head(patients)
starting_betas = startingBetaEstimation(x=patients,K=3:12,background_signature=background)
lambda_range = lambdaRangeBetaEvaluation(x=patients,K=10,beta=starting_betas[[8,1]], lambda_values=c(0.05,0.10))
data(starting_betas_example)
data(lambda_range_example)
cv = nmfLassoCV(x=patients,K=3:10)
data(cv_example)
beta = starting_betas_example[["5_signatures","Value"]]
res = nmfLasso(x = patients, K = 5, beta = beta, background_signature = background, seed = 12345)
data(nmf_LassoK_example)
signatures = nmf_LassoK_example$beta
signatures.plot(beta=signatures, xlabels=FALSE)
